To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mental and behavioral disorders account, globally, for about 1/3 of the burden of disability and are projected to become the leading cause of ill health and death by 2030, and that a range of evidence based cost-effective interventions exist that can be implemented to reduce the silent burden of mental disorders.
mental and behavioral disorders are the leading cause of the global burden of disease, and that the burden of disease can be reduced by implementing cost-effective evidence-based interventions.

the global burden of mental and substance use disorders is large and increasing and that the burden can be substantially reduced by implementing evidence-based cost-effective mental health interventions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) the development of a new methodological approach to the analysis of mental health and well-being data; (ii) the use of the methodological approach to understand and explain the determinants of mental health and wellbeing; and (iii) the application of the methodological and empirical findings in policy analysis and policy development.
the promotion of positive mental health and the prevention and treatment of mental disorders.
the promotion of mental health, the reduction of mental disorders, and the improvement of mental well-being.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mental disorders account for one third of the global burden of ill health and premature death, and the burden of mental disorders is increasing in all countries.
the mental health and well-being of all people is a fundamental human right and that it is a global public health priority.
mental health is a global priority that requires urgent action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the world needs to invest more in mental health and in the prevention of mental disorders, and we need to do so now.
we have shown that there is a strong case for investment in mental health promotion and prevention.
mental health promotion is a public good and should not be considered a private good.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the burden of impaired mental and behavioral health is large, and it is not being adequately addressed by governments and other stakeholders, including the private sector.
mental health is a key part of health.
there are many opportunities to reduce mental disorders, but they need to be better exploited and scaled up.
